name: terminal-animation

frames.best_why: The new tab is full of coloured scaffolding output, showing the typed command and the result together.
frames.render_note: The terminal window runs past the bottom edge of every frame, so its lower half is never shown.

tagline: A browser-window terminal types commands and streams coloured output.
summary: A fake terminal window with traffic-light dots and tabs for commands like new, dev, test and build. It retypes the command for the chosen tab, then prints its coloured output line by line behind a blinking cursor.
appearance: A dark rounded terminal window with three coloured dots and a row of six text tabs at the top, filled with a large monospaced command line and output lines. It floats on a violet-to-indigo gradient backdrop that darkens toward the edges.
behaviour: Picking a tab retypes that tab's command character by character, then reveals its output lines one after another with timed pauses; the cursor blinks while typing and disappears once output finishes. The whole window also slides up into place when it first scrolls into view.
demo_content: Tabs new, dev, lint, fmt, test, build showing Vite scaffolding, server, lint and test output.
search_phrases: animated console output for landing page
macos terminal window with traffic light dots
use_when: A landing page or portfolio wants to show a product or developer workflow inside a familiar terminal.
avoid_when: The window forces a dark surface that clashes on light pages, and each tab's output text is written into the source.
customise: Pass a tabs array of label, command and coloured lines; active tab, background image, forced dark and cursor hiding are props. Window styling and layout are file edits.
weight_why: A few dozen text lines revealed by timers; no canvas or heavy loop.

a11y.note: The tab list and output log are labelled for screen readers, but tabs are not tied to a panel and the slide-up ignores reduced-motion.

issues: Every frame crops the terminal window at the bottom, so its full height and output are never seen.
Frame 5 catches the reset between tabs and shows an almost empty window.
polish_why: Typed commands and coloured output sell the effect; the recording never shows the window whole.
